sentences.text:
1 C.S.C. 
 Court No. - 29  HON'BLE MAHESH CHANDRA TRIPATHI, J. 
HON'BLE KUNAL RAVI SINGH, J. 1.
Heard Shri Umesh Vats, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Shri Rakesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the petitioners and Shri N.K. Pandey, learned Standing Counsel for State respondents.

2. The instant writ petition has been preferred for following reliefs:-
"(I) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents authorities not to construct any road over the private land of the petitioners, without paying any compensation.
(II) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent authorities to decide the claim of the petitioner in pursuance of the Government Order dated 12.05.2016 and 25.07.2024."

3. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are owners with transferable right over Gata No.151/2 having area 0.6840 hect. situated in Village Daurau Chandpur, Tehsil Gabhana, Distt. Aligarh, which is evident from the relevant Khatauni (Annexure No.1).

He has placed reliance on the Government Order dated 21.6.2024, which has been issued pursuant to order dated 25.5.2023 in Writ-C No.4161 of 2023 (Harveer v. State of U.P. & Ors.),
whereby the State machinery was directed that no illegal or unauthorized occupation shall be made over the private land of any person except in accordance with law.

entities.text: Harveer v. State of U.P. & Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is alleged that in arbitrary manner in the guise of road widening the respondents are encroaching upon the petitioner's holding without any adequate compensation.

He fairly submits that the petitioners are not inclined to hamper the work but at the same time the respondents may be directed to ensure adequate compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short the 'Act 2013').
4.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Standing Counsel submits that highly disputed facts have been raised in the instant writ petition, which cannot be settled under Art.226 of the Constitution of India.

However,
he informed to the Court that for redressal of grievance of tenure holders, claiming certain right/title over their land, the State Government had issued detailed Government Order dated 12.05.2016, which provides that in case the claimant files claim supported with requisite documents,
the same would be considered by the District Level Committee for ensuring adequate compensation in the light of Act 2013.

He submits that once the efficacious remedy is available to the petitioners,
the matter should be relegated to the District Level Committee, which may examine the claim of petitioners within a reasonable time and submit its report to the Chairman/District Magistrate, who Smt Ramwati Devi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10929357/
2 may accord adequate compensation accordingly.

entities.text: Ramwati Devi And Another vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the relief prayed in the instant matter, we dispose of the instant petition with liberty to the petitioners to make fresh representation along with certified copy of the instant order before District Level Committee constituted under the Government Order dated 12.05.2016 within two weeks.

In the event, such representation is made,
the District Level Committee shall consider the claim of the petitioners and ensure that the proceeding shall be finalised expeditiously, preferably within twelve weeks, thereafter.

(Kunal Ravi Singh,J.) (Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.) November 7, 2025 SP/
